newsitem.title: USA: Conn. mulls early retirement for state employees.
newsitem.headline: Conn. mulls early retirement for state employees.

text.p: Connecticut Governor John Rowland said Thursday he had asked his labor negotiating team to hold talks with State Employee Bargaining Agent Coalition (SEBAC) leaders on an early retirement plan for state workers.
"It is clear that as we continue to restructure state government, the size and composition of our workforce must change substantially," Rowland said in a statement.
Rowland, a Republican, has said for some time he would like to downsize state government to make it leaner and more efficient.
But Thursday's announcement was the first time Rowland indicated he would like an early retirement package to be negotiated and offered to state employees.
"The recently concluded agreement with SEBAC on pension and medical benefits gives me reason to believe our efforts on an early retirement package will also be successful," said Rowland.
It is estimated that the Feb 3 contract agreement with SEBAC will lead to savings of more than $260 million over the next three years.
The agreement locks in pension plans until the year 2017 and creates a Tier IIA for new employees requiring a 2 percent co-pay and 5 percent co-pay for hazardous duty employees.
